# Modeling {#sec-modeling blurb="How the diagnostic classification models are specified, estimated, and evaluated."}

```{r}
#| label: setup-modeling
source("_common.R")
```

The DLM assessments are scored with diagnostic classification models [DCMs\; @rupp2010]. Rather than placing students on a continuous scale, DCMs estimate the probability that a student has mastered each linkage level of each Essential Element. This chapter describes the model, the estimation procedure, and the evaluation of model fit.

## The Model {#sec-model}

Each linkage level is calibrated with a log-linear cognitive diagnosis model [LCDM\; @henson2009] that measures a single attribute. For item $i$ and a student with mastery status $\alpha \in \{0, 1\}$, the probability of a correct response is given by @eq-lcdm.

$$
P(X_i = 1 \mid \alpha) = \frac{\exp(\lambda_{i,0} + \lambda_{i,1}\alpha)}{1 + \exp(\lambda_{i,0} + \lambda_{i,1}\alpha)}
$$ {#eq-lcdm}

The intercept $\lambda_{i,0}$ determines the probability of a correct response for a nonmaster, and the main effect $\lambda_{i,1}$ is the increase in log-odds associated with mastery. Models are estimated with the **measr** package [@measr].

::: {.callout-important}
## Fungible item parameters

When items measuring a linkage level are fungible, a single intercept and main effect are estimated for all items. The fungible model reduces the number of parameters substantially for linkage levels with small samples.
:::

## Parameter Estimates {#sec-parameters}

@fig-params shows the distribution of estimated item parameters for nonmasters and masters across all linkage levels. @tbl-params summarizes the estimates by linkage level.

```{r}
#| label: fig-params
#| fig-cap: "Estimated probability of a correct response for masters and nonmasters (simulated)"
#| fig-alt: "Density plot of the probability of a correct response. Nonmasters cluster near 0.3 and masters cluster near 0.85."
set.seed(3)
params <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("Nonmasters", "Masters"), each = 800),
  p = c(rbeta(800, 3, 7), rbeta(800, 12, 2.2))
)
ggplot(params, aes(x = p, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.85, colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = dlm_palette(c("sky", "navy")),
    breaks = c("Nonmasters", "Masters")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Probability of a correct response", y = "Density", fill = NULL) +
  theme_dlm()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-params
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of item parameter estimates by linkage level (simulated)"
levels <- c(
  "Initial Precursor",
  "Distal Precursor",
  "Proximal Precursor",
  "Target",
  "Successor"
)
tab <- data.frame(
  `Linkage level` = levels,
  `Items` = sample(300:900, 5),
  `Nonmaster mean` = sort(runif(5, .18, .35)),
  `Nonmaster SD` = runif(5, .08, .14),
  `Master mean` = sort(runif(5, .78, .9), decreasing = TRUE),
  `Master SD` = runif(5, .06, .12),
  check.names = FALSE
)
gt(tab) |>
  fmt_integer(Items) |>
  fmt_number(-c(`Linkage level`, Items), decimals = 2)
```

## Model Fit {#sec-model-fit}

Absolute fit is evaluated with posterior predictive model checks [@park2015]. Relative fit compares the fungible and nonfungible models using leave-one-out cross-validation. @tbl-fit lists the fit flags for each Essential Element. The table is long by design so the PDF demonstrates a table breaking across pages with a repeated header.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fit
#| tbl-cap: "Model fit flags by Essential Element and linkage level (simulated)"
ee <- sprintf(
  "M.EE.%d.%s.%d",
  rep(3:8, each = 6),
  rep(c("NS", "OA", "G", "MD", "SP", "EE"), 6),
  rep(1:2, 18)
)
fit <- data.frame(
  `Essential Element` = ee,
  `IP` = sample(c("✓", "✓", "✓", "Flag"), length(ee), TRUE),
  `DP` = sample(c("✓", "✓", "✓", "Flag"), length(ee), TRUE),
  `PP` = sample(c("✓", "✓", "✓", "✓", "Flag"), length(ee), TRUE),
  `T` = sample(c("✓", "✓", "✓", "✓", "Flag"), length(ee), TRUE),
  `S` = sample(c("✓", "✓", "✓", "Flag"), length(ee), TRUE),
  `ppp` = runif(length(ee), .05, .95),
  check.names = FALSE
)
gt(fit) |>
  fmt_number(ppp, decimals = 3) |>
  cols_align("center", columns = IP:S)
```
